decisions.reason: As a core airfield-lighting control product with a prominent launch and likely high development and certification costs, management is inclined to stay committed and treat any weak uptake as temporary airport-market weakness.
The surveillance display is close to the firm's airport-systems business and was given visible website support, so sunk costs and the need to justify the launch favor continuation.

Although a training program is easier to discontinue than hardware, it complements the installed base and disappointing demand can plausibly be blamed on temporary post-pandemic delays in airport training budgets.

This training course appears less prominently committed, is relatively low-cost to exit, and is peripheral enough that management can cut it while still preserving commitment to the more strategic product lines.

The collaboration software tool signals a strategic digital extension around airport operations, and its dedicated presentation makes management more likely to persist rather than admit an early retreat.

The multilateration surveillance system involved a highly public launch, substantial technical investment, and a strong fit with airport systems, all of which strongly encourage escalation of commitment and continued support.
